Chapter 18
Diseases of the Renal System  525
In a person with CKD, the normal PTH feedback loop is 
disabled, as shown in Figure 18.4. Damaged kidneys no longer 
have the ability to convert inactive vitamin D into active 
calcitriol, thus limiting calcium absorption from the intestine.
Additionally, damaged kidneys may not be able to reabsorb 
calcium and excrete phosphorus, leading to an imbalance in
the blood. Phosphorus is excreted primarily in the urine (about
500 to 1,400 mg/day), and to a lesser degree in the feces (about 
200 to 600 mg/day). Reabsorption of phosphorus in the renal 
tubules is the main mechanism by which the body maintains a
